{{short description|Indian chemist (born 1971)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2018}}
{{Use Indian English|date=October 2018}}
'''Souvik Maiti''' (born in 1971) is an Indian chemist known for his studies in the fields of biophysical chemistry and chemical biology focusing on nucleic acids, DNA and RNA.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=496 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | access-date=18 October 2016}}</ref> He works at the [[Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology]]. He is also visiting scientist at National Chemical Laboratory Pune and Adjunct Professor at IISER Mohali.

== Education ==
He graduated with a bachelor's (1993) and master's (1995) degree in chemistry from [[Jadavpur University]], Kolkata. He completed his doctoral research in 1999 in the field of polymer chemistry from CSIR-[[Indian Institute of Chemical Technology]], Hyderabad.

== Leadership Role == 
Souvik Maiti serves as the Director https://www.igib.res.in/Administration-&-Technical-Staff for the institute, CSIR-Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology, New Delhi.

== Research ==
He is known for his studies on biophysical aspect of quadruplexes, locked nucleic acids. He is also known for his work on silencing microRNAs by small molecules. His group has invented nucleic acid-based enzyme as silencers for microRNA, known as antagomirzymes.<ref name="Antagomirzymes: oligonucleotide enzymes that specifically silence microRNA function">{{Cite journal|pmid = 19229913|year = 2009|last1 = Jadhav|first1 = V. M.|last2 = Scaria|first2 = V.|last3 = Maiti|first3 = S.|title = Antagomirzymes: Oligonucleotide enzymes that specifically silence microRNA function|journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English|volume = 48|issue = 14|pages = 2557–2560|doi = 10.1002/anie.200805521 | bibcode=2009ACIE...48.2557J }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jadhav |first1=Vaibhav M. |last2=Scaria |first2=Vinod |last3=Maiti |first3=Souvik |date=2009 |title=Antagomirzymes: oligonucleotide enzymes that specifically silence microRNA function |journal=Angewandte Chemie (International ed. In English) |volume=48 |issue=14 |pages=2557–2560 |doi=10.1002/anie.200805521 |issn=1521-3773 |pmid=19229913 |bibcode=2009ACIE...48.2557J }}</ref> He is recipient of CSIR, NASI-Scopus, CDRI, AVRA Young Scientist Awards and Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award in Chemistry, [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology|Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar award]]s in 2014.,<ref>{{cite web|title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar awards for 10 scientists |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/states/shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-awards-for-10-scientists/article6450071.ece |publisher=BusinessLine |date=26 September 2014 |access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. P.S.Ahuja Announces Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award 2014 |url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=110063 |publisher=Dr. P.S.Ahuja Announces Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award 2014 |date=26 September 2014|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/WriteReadData/LatestUpdates/201409260153504671808ssb_awardees2014.pdf | title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science & Technology 2014 List of recipients | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | access-date=29 October 2018 }}</ref> [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]] of the [[Department of Biotechnology]] in 2015.<ref name="N-BIOS awardees 2015">{{cite web | url=http://www.dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/bioscience-award.pdf | title=N-BIOS awardees 2015 | publisher=Department of Biotechnology | date=2016 | access-date=18 October 2016}}</ref> in Biology, as well as Swarnajayanti Fellowships in Biological Sciences. He is fellow of Indian Academy of Sciences, Bangalore, and Indian National Academy of Science, Delhi.

Souvik Maiti and Debojyoti Chakraborty, have jointly led development of an indigenous CRISPR gene-editing platform based on an engineered variant of Cas9 known as enFnCas9/FnCas9, developed to build a clinically viable pathway for translating genome-editing therapies within India's scientific and public health context. 

Along with his colleague, Debojyoti Chakraborty, he has co-invented a rapid test for COVID-19, FnCas9 Editor-Linked Uniform Detection Assay, FELUDA.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/low-cost-feluda-test-to-detect-virus-in-an-hour-likely-in-4-weeks/story-q1Q8ATDRNnwEGuRbhWVI2O.html|title=Low-cost 'Feluda' test to detect virus in an hour likely in 4 weeks|date=13 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/lifestyle/health/covid-19-test-result-in-minutes-feluda-indias-first-paper-strip-test-check-details/1949771/|title=COVID-19 test result in minutes! 'Feluda' India's first paper strip test; check details|date=6 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/change-in-icmr-rules-stalls-covid-19-test-kits-from-government-labs/article31900038.ece|title=Change in ICMR rules stalls COVID-19 test kits from government labs|newspaper=The Hindu|date=23 June 2020|last1=Koshy|first1=Jacob}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/covid-19-outbreak-csir-develops-low-cost-paper-based-30-minute-testing-kit-feluda/videoshow/75585647.cms |title=COVID-19 outbreak: CSIR develops low-cost, paper-based, 30-minute testing kit 'Feluda' - the Economic Times Video &#124; ET Now |access-date=17 July 2020 |archive-date=7 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807102814/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/covid-19-outbreak-csir-develops-low-cost-paper-based-30-minute-testing-kit-feluda/videoshow/75585647.cms |url-status=dead }}</ref> (named after [[Feluda]], a popular fictional detective created by the late [[Satyajit Ray]].) [[Tata Sons]] has obtained license from CSIR for commercial launch of this test.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theprint.in/science/tata-sons-to-help-make-feluda-csirs-satyajit-ray-inspired-covid-paper-test-kit/416390/|title=Tata Sons to help make 'Feluda', CSIR's Satyajit Ray-inspired Covid paper test kit|website=[[ThePrint]] |date=7 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tata Sons to Scale-up Covid-19 Testing Kit 'Feluda' |url=https://vigyanprasar.gov.in/isw/Tata-Sons-to-Scale-up-Covid-19-Testing-Kit-Feluda.html |access-date=2023-08-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.themachinemaker.com/innovation/covid19-test-kit-feluda-dr-debojyoti-chakraborty|title = &#124; the Machine Maker| date=9 May 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/made-in-india-paper-based-strip-for-rapid-mass-testing/articleshow/75566159.cms|title = Feluda Test Kit: Made-in-India paper-based strip for rapid, mass testing for Covid-19 &#124; India News - Times of India|website = [[The Times of India]]| date=6 May 2020 }}</ref> Tata group has established a new company, TATA MD and launched this test as a brand name "TATA MD Check". In 2021, CSIR and Tata MD partner to ramp up COVID testing capacity across tier 2, 3 towns and rural areas.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/healthcare/tatamd-anderson-diagnostic-labs-partner-to-detect-new-covid-19-variants/articleshow/81635044.cms | title=TataMD & ADL partner to transform COVID testing thru' TataMD CHECK | newspaper=The Economic Times }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/healthcare/csir-tata-md-partner-to-ramp-up-covid-testing-capacity-across-tier-2-3-towns-and-rural-areas/articleshow/83636670.cms | title=CSIR, Tata MD partner to ramp up Covid testing capacity across tier 2, 3 towns and rural areas | newspaper=The Economic Times | access-date=2024-03-03 | date=2021-06-18}}</ref>

Building on this platform, the two researchers developed BIRSA 101 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2261232&reg=48&lang=2, described as India's first indigenous CRISPR-based gene therapy for sickle cell disease.The therapy was launched with a technology transfer and collaboration agreement between CSIR-IGIB and the Serum Institute of India, enabling large-scale, cost-effective production of CRISPR therapies for sickle cell disease and other genetic disorders. The therapy is named after tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda and targets sickle cell disease, which disproportionately affects India's tribal populations. It aims to offer a potentially permanent cure at a fraction of the cost of existing global CRISPR-based therapies, which run into millions of dollars
